questions.q: What is the accounting equation?
questions.why: Everything the business owns is financed by the owner or by others.

questions.q: Which is a liability?
questions.why: A liability is an amount the business owes.

questions.q: Which is the accounting equation?
questions.why: It always balances.

questions.q: A business has assets of $85 000 and liabilities of $23 000. What is the owner's capital?
questions.why: Capital = Assets − Liabilities, so 85 000 − 23 000 = $62 000.

questions.q: The owner takes $500 cash from the business for personal use. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
questions.why: Drawings reduce cash (an asset) and reduce the owner's capital by the same amount, so the equation still balances.

questions.q: Which document is sent by a seller to request payment?
questions.why: A credit note reduces the amount owed, e.g. for returns.

questions.q: In double entry, buying goods on credit is recorded as…
questions.why: Purchases increase (debit); the amount owed to the supplier increases (credit).

questions.q: Which is the book of prime entry for credit sales?
questions.why: Cash sales go in the cash book.

questions.q: A trader pays a credit supplier $400 by cheque. What is the double entry?
questions.why: The amount owed (a liability) falls, so the supplier is debited; the bank balance falls, so bank is credited.

questions.q: Goods with a list price of $2 000 are sold on credit less 10% trade discount. What amount is entered in the sales journal?
questions.why: Trade discount is deducted on the invoice and never recorded in the ledger, so only the net $1 800 is entered.

long.q: State the difference between an invoice and a credit note.
scheme: B1: an invoice is sent by the seller to a credit customer, showing the amount owed for goods sold
B1: a credit note is sent by the seller to reduce the amount owed, e.g. for returned or faulty goods

questions.q: Which error does NOT affect the trial balance?
o: Entry on the wrong side of one account only
questions.why: Commission errors post to the wrong account of the right type; debits still equal credits.

questions.q: A bank reconciliation explains differences between…
o: the cash book and the bank statement
questions.why: Timing differences like unpresented cheques cause them.

questions.q: Which error does not affect the agreement of the trial balance?
o: Entering different amounts on each side
questions.why: Errors of commission, omission, principle, original entry, reversal and complete reversal don't show in the trial balance.

questions.q: A cash book shows a debit (favourable) bank balance of $3 000. The bank statement shows bank charges of $40 not yet in the cash book. What is the updated cash book balance?
questions.why: Bank charges reduce the money in the bank, so they are credited in the cash book: 3 000 − 40 = $2 960.

questions.q: Repairs of $300 to a delivery van were debited to the motor vehicles account. What type of error is this?
questions.why: Revenue expenditure was posted to a non-current asset account, the wrong class of account, which is an error of principle.

questions.q: A machine costs $10 000, lasts 5 years and has no residual value. What is straight-line depreciation per year?
questions.why: (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life = 10 000 ÷ 5.

questions.q: Prepaid expenses are shown as…
questions.why: They are paid in advance for a future period.

questions.q: Writing off an irrecoverable debt…
questions.why: It is an expense in the income statement.

questions.q: Inventory items: A cost $50, NRV $40; B cost $30, NRV $45. At what value should inventory be shown?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some compared total cost with total NRV. Apply lower of cost and NRV to each item: 40 + 30 = $70.

questions.q: Annual rent is $6 000. During the year the business paid $5 500. What rent expense is charged in the income statement?
questions.why: The accruals principle charges the full year's cost of $6 000; the unpaid $500 is shown as an accrued expense (a current liability).

long.q: A van cost $12 000 and is expected to last 5 years, with a residual value of $2000. Calculate the annual depreciation using the straight-line method and the net book value after 2 years.
scheme: A1: net book value after 2 years = $8000

questions.q: Revenue $50 000, cost of sales $30 000. What is gross profit?
questions.why: Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales.

questions.q: Cost of sales is calculated as…
questions.why: It is the cost of the goods actually sold in the period.

questions.q: A club buys new furniture. Where is this shown?
o: Statement of financial position as a non-current asset
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some put the furniture in the income and expenditure account; it is capital expenditure.

questions.q: Gross profit is $32 000, expenses are $19 000 and rent received is $1 500. What is the profit for the year?
questions.why: Profit for the year = gross profit + other income − expenses = 32 000 + 1 500 − 19 000 = $14 500.

questions.q: In a partnership's financial statements, where is interest on partners' capital shown?
o: Statement of financial position as a current liability
Trading account as part of cost of sales
questions.why: Interest on capital is a share of profit to the partners, not a business expense, so it goes in the appropriation account.

long.q: Revenue was $80 000. Opening inventory was $6000, purchases $50 000 and closing inventory $8000. Calculate the cost of sales and the gross profit.

questions.q: Gross profit $20 000 on revenue $80 000. What is the gross margin?
A quick (acid test) ratio excludes…
questions.why: Inventory may be slow to turn into cash.

questions.q: What does the current ratio measure?
o: Whether a business can pay its short-term debts
questions.why: Current assets ÷ current liabilities.

questions.q: Revenue is $120 000 and profit for the year is $18 000. What is the profit margin?
questions.why: Profit margin = profit for the year ÷ revenue × 100 = 18 000 ÷ 120 000 × 100 = 15%.

questions.q: Cost of sales is $60 000 and average inventory is $7 500. What is the rate of inventory turnover?
questions.why: Rate of inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory = 60 000 ÷ 7 500 = 8 times a year.

long.q: A trader has current assets of $18 000 and current liabilities of $12 000. Calculate the current ratio and comment on it.
scheme: B1: comment, e.g. the business can cover its short-term debts, though below the 2 : 1 often suggested

questions.q: Which principle says revenue is recorded when earned, not when cash is received?
questions.why: Income and expenses are matched to the period they relate to.

questions.q: Prudence means…
questions.why: Accountants shouldn't anticipate gains, but should provide for likely losses.

questions.q: Which concept says a business records assets at cost, not what they'd fetch today?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many could name prudence but struggled to suggest another reason.

questions.q: A business keeps using straight-line depreciation every year instead of switching methods to make profit look higher. Which principle is it following?
questions.why: Consistency means using the same methods from year to year so that results can be compared fairly.

questions.q: The owner pays her home electricity bill from the business bank account. The bookkeeper records it as drawings, not as a business expense. Which principle is applied?
questions.why: The business is treated as separate from its owner, so the owner's private spending is drawings, not a business cost.
